hints: Look first for what is missing in the high wavenumber region, as broad absorptions tell you about O-H groups.
Notice the very strong, sharp dip at about 1700 cm-1, which is characteristic of a particular double bond.
Combine the absence of any broad O-H with the presence of that carbonyl plus strong peaks at 1000-1300 cm-1 to pick the functional group.
walkthrough:
**Check for O-H above 2500 cm-1**

Look at the left side of the spectrum. There is no broad dip around 3200-3600 cm-1 for an alcohol, and no very broad dip from 2500-3300 cm-1 for a carboxylic acid. So G has no O-H group.

Rule: $\text{O-H (alcohol): broad } 3200-3600 \text{ cm}^{-1}$, $\text{O-H (acid): very broad } 2500-3300 \text{ cm}^{-1}$

**Spot the carbonyl C=O**

There is a very strong, sharp absorption at about 1700-1750 cm-1. That is the classic C=O stretch of a ketone, aldehyde, acid or ester.

Rule: $$\text{C=O stretch } \approx 1680-1750 \text{ cm}^{-1} \text{ (strong, sharp)}$$

**Use the fingerprint C-O region to confirm ester**

The spectrum also shows strong sharp peaks in the 1000-1300 cm-1 region for C-O single bonds. A carbonyl with C-O but no O-H points to an ester.

Logic: $\text{C=O present + C-O present + O-H absent} = \text{ester}$

**Match to the options**

Only $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$, methyl ethanoate, is an ester with no O-H. The others all either contain O-H or lack C=O.

options.A: Incorrect. CH3COCH2OH is a hydroxy-ketone. It has C=O so would show the 1700 cm-1 peak, but it also has an alcohol O-H which should give a broad absorption at 3200-3600 cm-1. That broad peak is absent.
options.B: Incorrect. CH3CH2CO2H is propanoic acid, a carboxylic acid. It would show C=O, but also a very broad O-H absorption covering 2500-3300 cm-1. The spectrum is flat with high transmittance there, so this is ruled out.
options.C: Correct. CH3CO2CH3 is methyl ethanoate, an ester. It fits perfectly: strong sharp C=O at about 1740 cm-1, strong C-O absorptions at 1000-1300 cm-1, C-H just below 3000 cm-1, and no broad O-H absorption.
options.D: Incorrect. CH3CHCHCH3 is but-2-ene, a hydrocarbon alkene. It has no C=O group, so it cannot give the very strong sharp peak at about 1700 cm-1. It also cannot give strong C-O peaks.
